scenes.headline: The Cluster Manager
scenes.subtitle: The resource negotiator that launches driver and executors.
scenes.narration: The cluster manager is the layer that allocates machines and memory so your Spark application can run.

scenes.headline: What it handles
items: Accepts the application submission and its resource request
Allocates CPU cores and memory across the cluster
Launches the executor processes on worker nodes
Reclaims resources when the application finishes
scenes.narration: The cluster manager accepts your application and its resource request. It allocates CPU and memory across the cluster, launches executor processes on worker nodes, and reclaims those resources once the job is done.

scenes.headline: Common cluster managers

columns.title: Standalone / YARN
points: YARN is common in Hadoop clusters

scenes.narration: Spark supports several managers. Standalone and YARN are mature choices common in Hadoop environments, while Kubernetes runs executors as pods and is the cloud-native, elastic option for modern platforms.

scenes.headline: Choosing the manager with master
scenes.narration: The master setting tells Spark which cluster manager to use. Here we target YARN, but the same code can point to Kubernetes, a standalone master, or local mode for testing on your laptop.

scenes.text: Spark's engine is the same everywhere; the cluster manager just decides how resources are provided.
scenes.narration: The important point is that Spark's engine stays the same across environments — the cluster manager only changes how resources are provided.
